text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — KV cache metadata growth > 85% in paged blockmgr (region: us-west-2). Continuous batching rate spiked. Potential customer latency impact. Auto-escalation to oncall 15:03 UTC.

maria_k: saw the alert, i'm on it. looking at the blockmgr metrics now.

sam_r: thanks — i'm tying this to the continuous batching roll that shipped ~14:45. canary looked fine but throughput changed traffic patterns.

maria_k: logs show a growing number of partial blocks stuck in 'pinned' state, eviction loop not reclaiming. sample log: ```
2026-03-15T14:58:12Z blockmgr: block_id=0x7f4 pinned=true last_access=2026-03-15T14:40:01Z metadata_bytes=8192
2026-03-15T14:58:12Z eviction: considered=12 evicted=0 reason=pin_conflict
```

derek_o: that fits a metadata leak pattern — some code path may be pinning blocks for the duration of a batched request and not releasing on early abort.

carla_p: customers reporting 5-10x tail latency for embeddings and chat requests. i've opened a couple support tickets and flagged priority.

maria_k: immediate mitigations I can roll: 1) throttle continuous batching to safe floor (batch_size cap), 2) enable aggressive background eviction for paged blockmgr for 30 mins, 3) revert canary if needed. leaning to 1+2 first to avoid full revert.

sam_r: agree. we want minimal customer impact. do we have a validated flag to toggle batch size quickly?

derek_o: yes — runtime config: `/configs/continuous_batching.json` has `max_batch_tokens` and `batch_window_ms`. i can push a hotfix to reduce `max_batch_tokens` from 4096 -> 1024 and `batch_window_ms` from 50 -> 20.

maria_k: can you prepare the change and a canary rollout to 5% of traffic? we need to watch metadata_bytes metric.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT REQUEST by derek_o: PATCH /configs/continuous_batching.json {"max_batch_tokens":1024,"batch_window_ms":20} -> canary 5% at 15:12 UTC.

sam_r: also add a temporary eviction tweak: set `blockmgr.eviction.aggressiveness = high` and `blockmgr.max_pinned_age_ms = 60000` so pinned blocks older than 60s can be reclaimed (with caution).

carla_p: note: aggressive eviction can cause more IO spikes — will warn customers SRE-side. but i'm +1 if it drops metadata growth quickly.

maria_k: i'm going to run the canary now. monitoring: `kv.metadata_bytes_total`, `blockmgr.pinned_count`, `request_tail_latency_p99`. will post updates.

15:14 maria_k: canary deployed to 5%. initial green. metadata growth slope reduced but still trending up. pinned_count down 12% in first 2 minutes.

15:17 derek_o: pushed eviction flags to high for the control plane. small IO increase visible but metadata growth stalled. p99 latency improving for the canary segment.

15:22 sam_r: good. let's ramp canary to 25% over 5 minutes and continue to monitor.

15:28 maria_k: ramp to 25% done. overall pinned_count down 35% vs peak. global request p99 reduced from 680ms -> 220ms for affected cluster.

carla_p: support update sent to customers A, B, C: "we're seeing degraded tails due to a KV cache metadata growth issue caused by a recent batching change. we've throttled batching and adjusted eviction; we're monitoring and will provide updates."

15:35 ops-bot: ALERT — regression guard: error_rate spike to 0.9% in canary.

15:36 derek_o: investigating error spike — looks like a rare race in the unpin path under the new batch limits causing transient 503s for short-lived requests. rolling a tiny rollback of `batch_window_ms` to 30 for canary only.

15:40 maria_k: after rollback to 30ms in canary, error_rate back to baseline. pinned_count still trending down. i'm going to continue ramp but keep batch_window_ms at 30ms globally until we patch the pin/unpin race.

15:47 sam_r: plan for next steps: 1) ship a small fix to release pins on early abort (derek to code), 2) keep batching caps conservative for 12 hours, 3) leave eviction aggressiveness high for 30 mins then step to medium, 4) prepare postmortem.

derek_o: i have a repro — adding a try/finally around the pin section fixes it. will open PR and request expedited review.

15:58 ops-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF scheduled — current oncall: maria_k -> next oncall: lee_t at 16:00 UTC.

maria_k: handoff notes for lee_t: issue was KV metadata blowup due to continuous batching exposing a pin/unpin race in paged blockmgr. mitigations applied: capped `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 (global), `batch_window_ms` set to 30ms (global), eviction aggressiveness set to high (auto-deescalate in 30m). watch `kv.metadata_bytes_total`, `blockmgr.pinned_count`, and customer p99. PR #4826 fixes the leak; target deploy in 2 hours after tests.

lee_t: acknowledged, i'll take over monitoring. any outstanding customer escalations?

carla_p: two priority tickets still open (A & B) — i've assigned interim compensations and provided timeline. will update after PR merge.

16:05 lee_t: quick check-in — metrics holding, pinned_count steady, p99 stable ~230ms. i'll keep the eviction flag until 16:30 and then step down to medium if no recrudescence. leaving the channel but ping me if things change.

maria_k: thanks team. postmortem action items: - test coverage for pin/unpin race - add telemetry for pinned duration histogram - safer default batch caps in runtime - ops-runbook update for paged blockmgr escalations.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (status: mitigated). root cause: pin/unpin race triggered by higher sustained batch sizes. next steps: follow the action items.

carla_p: i'll draft the customer update and the support-resolution notes.

lee_t: closing loop — PR merged and deployed 17:40 UTC, metrics normal. final customer notifications sent.

maria_k: great job everyone :thumbsup:
